**The solution is to give Clanker a payment tool that completes purchases you approve through Slack.**

The current block comes from our implementation: Clanker’s policy says payment is owner-only, and its payment handlers are disabled. The old card executor was removed during the Kernel migration. Sending you back to the sign-in link was also a broken checkout handoff. [Current policy](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/clanker_policy.py:4), [disabled handlers](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/payments.py:5).

Kernel **does support payments**, including protected card filling and wallet integrations. Clanker needs to integrate that capability. [Kernel payment documentation](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/browsers/payments).

The flow I recommend is:

1. **Clanker prepares checkout** and shows the verified merchant, items, delivery details and final total in Slack.
2. **You approve that exact purchase**, for example “Pay ₹69.” Approval belongs to your account and that checkout; changed totals require fresh approval.
3. **Clanker completes checkout** through Kernel’s payment integration. Card enrollment and any required bank authentication use a secure private link opened from Slack. You don’t operate Clanker’s browser.
4. **Clanker verifies the merchant’s order record** and returns the confirmation. An uncertain result triggers reconciliation before another payment attempt.

**For your India use case, I’d evaluate Kernel + AgentCard first.** It uses placeholder card values while the real card stays outside the agent’s browser, and Kernel documents support for specific Razorpay checkout requests. Kernel’s Link integration currently requires a US phone number. [AgentCard integration](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/integrations/wallets/agentcard), [Link requirements](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/integrations/wallets/stripe-link).

So saving a card alone won’t fix this. We need the wallet integration, purchase approval, payment execution and order verification together. The same approval flow can support COD when the merchant offers it.

**The remaining unknown is whether Zepto’s actual checkout matches a supported payment flow. That needs verification before promising it will work there.**

Yes, the Slack portion is straightforward with the current infrastructure. The missing work is the actual payment provider integration.

- **Pay ₹X button:** Existing Block Kit URL buttons already work in [service.py:424](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/service.py:424). Slack action registration currently only acknowledges clicks at [service.py:652](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/service.py:652). A URL button can open the payment page immediately; approval should be recorded by the authenticated payment page, never by the navigation GET alone.
- **Owner-only access:** Opaque links use random request IDs plus HMAC tokens, with workspace, owner, expiry and status validation in [store.py:154](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/store.py:154) and [store.py:160](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/store.py:160). Slack OIDC establishes the exact owner before returning the provider URL in [web.py:127](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/web.py:127). This can protect a channel-visible Pay card from other channel members.
- **Hosted redirect:** [web.py:138](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/web.py:138) already checks identity, then returns an external hosted form URL. [vault.js:37](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/vault.js:37) verifies provider hosts before redirecting. Payment providers need their own dedicated route and host validation.
- **Channel placement:** Current implementation deliberately delivers access links to DMs in [service.py:376](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/service.py:376), and rejects vault URLs in shared summaries at [channel_tasks.py:220](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/channel_tasks.py:220). A public Pay card needs a new generic opaque payment link, while card details remain private.
- **Payment gap:** All payment methods are disabled at [payments.py:19](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/payments.py:19), tools reject payment requests at [tools.py:16](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/tools.py:16), collection accepts only login/API-key requests at [kernel_service.py:745](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/kernel_service.py:745), and resumed payment requests also fail at [service.py:493](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/service.py:493).

Need to add: provider-hosted first-use card entry, optional provider-token persistence, transient card path when “remember” is unchecked, purchase-bound authorization, execution/reconciliation states, authenticated provider completion handling, and order verification. Existing `payment` schema remnants are not an implemented payment capability.

No secrets were read; no files, Slack messages, browser sessions or payment state were changed.
